summary: Perry County, PA bald tower used about 1909 to 1917 per the register; a 1908-09 forestry report describes a ranger's lookout at Chimney Rock; no longer standing; no site description found.

facts.design: Described only as a bald tower; no structure details given
facts.status_note: Register says it is no longer standing; no source describes what remains

events.note: 1908-09 report: a ranger living in Henry Valley used Chimney Rock to watch for fires

evidence.supports: bald tower used 1909 to about 1917; no longer standing
evidence.quote: This bald tower was used from 1909 to circa 1917 and is no longer standing.

evidence.supports: site is listed under the register as Chimney Rocks Tower Site (Perry County)
1908-09 report: rangers can view their divisions and locate fires
evidence.quote: From them rangers can view nearly all of their respective divisions, and would be able to locate any fire which might start.

evidence.supports: Chimney Rock on south side of Bower Mountain used by a ranger living in Henry Valley
evidence.quote: Chimney Rock, on the south side of Bower mountain, is used for the same purpose by the ranger living in Henry valley.

evidence.supports: the report is attributed to the Pennsylvania Department of Forestry
evidence.quote: (Report of the Pennsylvania Department of Forestry)

evidence.supports: the Forest Lookouts page files the report under its Perry County entry

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says Chimney Rocks; the 1908-09 report quoted by the Forest Lookouts page says Chimney Rock on Bower Mountain. The Forest Lookouts page places the report under its Perry County entry, so the story treats them as one site. That link comes only from the Forest Lookouts page.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: two pages, no build date, no structure description, no current-site source. The staffing item rests on the 1908-09 report quoted by Forest Lookouts, not on the register. A separate Franklin County Chimney Rocks (firetower.org US 241) and Blair County's Chimney Rocks Park are different places and were not used.
